findings.title: isAccessTokenId does not actually verify the encoded grant shortcut
findings.body: The new matcher checks `items[0].substring(3, 5).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)` and returns false when it matches. There are two defects: the grant shortcut occupies zero-based positions 4-5 (`substring(4, 6)`), not 3-4, and the condition is inverted. Consequently any access token id with a colon and a UUID suffix passes the matcher regardless of the encoded grant type, so the updated integration tests cannot catch wrong grant-type encoding. It should reject when the prefix length is not 6 or when `substring(4, 6)` is not equal to the expected shortcut.

findings.title: rawTokenId is never null-checked
findings.body: The constructor calls `Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, "Null rawTokenId not allowed")` a second time instead of checking `rawTokenId`. A null raw token id is therefore accepted, and `encodeTokenId` can later produce a malformed token id such as `onrtac:null`, defeating the constructor invariant. The second check should be `Objects.requireNonNull(rawTokenId, "Null rawTokenId not allowed")`.

findings.title: Grant shortcut length is not enforced even though the parser requires exactly two characters
findings.body: `encodeTokenId` concatenates the grant shortcut directly, while `getTokenContextFromTokenId` requires exactly 6 characters before the colon (lines 74-81). The new `OAuth2GrantTypeFactory#getShortcut()` contract does not require a two-character shortcut, and its Javadoc even says shortcuts are "usually like 3-letters". A custom grant returning a 3-character shortcut will make this server issue token ids like `onrtabc:...` that its own parser rejects with `IllegalArgumentException`, so the encoded context cannot be decoded. Validate that every grant shortcut is exactly two characters and contains no `:`, or make the parser length-aware.

findings.title: setFormParams leaves the cached grantType stale
findings.body: `Context.grantType` is derived from `formParams` in the constructor, but the public `setFormParams` setter replaces `formParams` without recomputing `grantType`. Any caller that mutates the form parameters will still get the old grant type from `getGrantType()`, and `OAuth2GrantTypeBase.createTokenResponse` will write that stale value into `clientSessionCtx`, causing the access token id to encode the wrong grant shortcut. Recompute `grantType` in `setFormParams` or avoid caching it as separate mutable state.
